title: The served-chain tie on a delta walk's result has no sentence in WTC-6 and no conformance row
description:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.ChainTie` (`tied` as current) refuses a delta walk whose resulting anchor
is not active on the view captured when the walk starts, even where the walk links from the cached
anchor and covers its range (`off_branch_walk_refused`). `WTC-6` has no sentence for that test: it
says "from a cached anchor whose block is still active" of the base, and "as is one that fails any
proof (`WTC-12`)" of the walk. The guard cites `WTC-11`'s "a block hash at a height that no longer
matches". ADR-0024 records that the reference implementation's `vault-node`,
`chain::advance_confirmed_scan` captures only a height when the walk starts and makes no such
test, and CNF-91 does not ask for it, so an implementation without the tie passes the checklist
while the model holds it as a rule.

Owner to decide: (1) the tie is `WTC-12`'s "the last is active after the loop" or `WTC-11`'s rule
applied to the walk's result, and the guard's citation and CNF-91 should say so; or (2) it needs
its own sentence in `WTC-6`; or (3) it is not required and the guard's current value is wrong.
Done when: the tie has a quoted Markdown home and a conformance row, or is withdrawn.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: M8: unbuilt wallet not latched, retries only at cold scans already needed, served-chain tie dropped, ancestry premise on views (delivers bps-8s0.11.22, .23, .24)
description:
Land three spec-owner decisions of 2026-10-02 in the Markdown and the Lean model in one commit.
Each was put to a four-adviser consultation (all four answered) and then
decided by the owner; no Consultation is needed. Delivers bps-8s0.11.22, bps-8s0.11.23 and
bps-8s0.11.24, which close with this bead.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/unbuilt-wallet.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends WTC-6 (its
pointer now reads "While the repair latch is set or a build or repair attempt is in progress"),
WTC-9 (rewritten lifecycle, below), WTC-11 (the wallet site: "a wallet that holds completion
markers none of whose anchors is still active") and CNF-91. Do not reword it; if a Lean-side fact
shows a sentence false, stop and say so in the report. The citation gate will report about 18
Lean quotations to move (VaultUnspent, Exhibits, Chain).

What WTC-9 now decides (bps-8s0.11.22):
- The latch applies only to a wallet that HOLDS a completion marker and none of whose markers is
  active. A wallet holding no marker (never built, or a first build that failed) is not latched;
  WTC-8 already keeps it out of use.
- STATE-BASED first scan: from the latch setting until a cold scan has replaced the cache, every
  refresh with no attempt in progress starts a repair attempt from a cold scan, whatever cache it
  holds. (A consultation found that "the first refresh after the latch sets" let a refresh after
  a failed first scan delta-walk from the pre-latch, possibly wallet-derived, cache.)
- Thereafter, while latched, the cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback, and
  a wallet read never replaces it.
- After a failed attempt, the next attempt starts ONLY from a cold scan WTC-6 itself reaches with
  none in progress, and starts no scan of its own. An unbuilt wallet's first build and its
  retries start the same way. Stated consequence: a failed build or repair is not retried while
  delta walks succeed; the cache does not depend on the wallet. (Owner's choice over a retained-
  scan retry and over reverting built wallets to retry every refresh.)

## 2. The Lean model

a. `observe` latches only a wallet with a non-empty marker list none of whose anchors is active;
   `no_marker_latches` inverts (an unbuilt wallet is not latched).
b. State records whether a cold scan has replaced the cache since the latch set (or equivalent).
   `refresh`: latched, no scan yet since the latch, no attempt in progress -> cold scan, start an
   attempt, whatever the cache; latched and scanned since -> delta walk with WTC-6's cold-scan
   fallback, and a fallback cold scan reached with no attempt in progress starts one; unlatched
   with no marker -> an attempt (first build) starts only from a cold scan WTC-6 reaches. A failed
   attempt starts no scan of its own.
c. Theorems: (i) a latched refresh before any post-latch scan cold-scans whatever the cache holds;
   (ii) after a failed attempt no refresh cold-scans unless WTC-6's own order reaches one (no
   storm); (iii) an unbuilt wallet never latches; (iv) an exhibit of the stated liveness
   consequence: a failed attempt followed by succeeding walks starts no new attempt.
d. Guard parameters, per AGENTS.md ("Every semantic choice a dated amendment changed is a guard
   parameter with a `current` value"), for: the latch's scope (`scoped` | `vacuous`) and the
   retry trigger (`neededScan` | `everyRefresh`), each with its twin trace, theorems over
   `current` in Exhibits.lean and a measured gates.yml control. Re-examine `LatchedBase`; merge or
   retire it if the new parameters subsume it, with the reason.
e. bps-8s0.11.24: `ChainTie`'s `current` becomes `untied`. All four advisers: WTC-12's "after the
   loop the hash at the last height still equals the last scanned hash" is the rule, compared with
   the chain after the walk, and the extra test against the view captured before the walk only
   discards a correct walk on a branch that reorged in just before it; WTC-5 already refuses any
   cache not at the current tip. Keep `tied` as the documented alternative with its exhibit;
   re-measure its CI control (the flip direction changes).
f. bps-8s0.11.23: in `Chain.lean`, beside `View`, a `Prop` on a pair (or an admissible family) of
   views: each view's tip is active in that view, and two views sharing an active block at height
   h agree at every height at or below h (a block hash commits to its ancestry). A HYPOTHESIS,
   never an axiom. `rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan` keeps its unconditional conclusion; add a
   corollary carrying the premise that proves the settled blocks of the recorded scan view and
   `scanView` are equal, so `rebuild` reads the attempt's settled block. `State`, `repair`,
   `rebuild` and the trace encoding do not change for this item. Keep the review probe (a scan on
   hashes [100, 101], a repair accepting [200, 101]) as an exhibit showing the premise excludes it.
g. If item b changes `State`'s encoding, bump the trace format version and record it in ADR-0023
   beside versions 2 and 3, with the reason.
h. Re-quote every broken quotation; re-measure every gates.yml control the change touches, alone,
   in a scratch copy, at exact counts.

## 3. Records

- ADR-0024: record the three decisions and their rejected alternatives briefly (a retained-scan
  retry; reverting built wallets to retry every refresh; recording the settled block in the
  attempt's state; keeping the served-chain tie as a new WTC-6 rule). Consequences: the reference
  does not latch an unseeded wallet (matches) but retries a failed latched repair on every pass
  (now diverges); the reference makes no served-chain tie (now matches).
- bps-8s0.11.14 (SEC-50): if its description quotes WTC-6 or WTC-9 text this patch changes,
  update it with `br update --description-file` to cite the current text.

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an
exact count; bps-8s0.11.22, .23 and .24 closed with this bead. NO commit message may carry a
Co-Authored-By trailer or a tool attribution. Out of scope: bps-8s0.11.16, bps-8s0.11.12.
close_reason: Delivered in 325c7bc. Nine gates green (Manager's own run, alone, unpiped, RC=0); gates.yml steps 37-42 pass at exact counts; four-reviewer Panel returned no findings.

title: M8: the first build has no scan-tie theorem, and latched-and-attempting-implies-scanned is not stated as an invariant
description:
From the review of bps-8s0.11.25 (commit 325c7bc). Two properties the model has by construction
but no theorem states, so a later edit could break either with every gate green.

1. The first build has no scan-tie theorem. `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan`
   and `rebuild_reads_the_attempts_settled_block` both take `st.latched = true`, so they cover a
   repair only. Since 325c7bc an unbuilt wallet's first build is an attempt that runs with the
   latch clear (`refresh` starts it at a served cold scan where `st.wallet.markers.isEmpty`), and
   `repair` holds it to its scan in code, but nothing proves it. Wanted: the sibling theorem keyed
   on `st.wallet.markers = []` and the wallet gaining a marker, with its corollary under
   `Chain.Ancestry`.

2. `failed_attempt_starts_no_scan` assumes `st.scanned = true`. Every latched attempt a refresh
   starts has it (`cold_scan_starts_attempt` sets it; `refresh`, `repair` and a latched
   `State.observe` keep it), but no theorem states `latched ∧ attempting → scanned` as an invariant
   preserved by `refresh`, `repair`, `endAsFailure` and `State.observe`. Wanted: the one-step
   preservation lemmas, so the "no scan storm" theorem's premise is discharged for every reachable
   state and the unreachable corner `latched ∧ ¬scanned ∧ attempting` (where `deltaBase` walks from
   the cache) is excluded rather than merely not produced.

No Markdown change; no guard parameter; no trace-format change. Done when both are proved, the
nine gates are green and any gates.yml control whose count moves is re-measured.

title: CI: run the gates workflow as four parallel jobs; the identifier controls skip the kernel replay
description:
The gates workflow takes about 32 minutes on the public runner: one job, every step in series. The owner
decided on 2026-10-02 to run it as four parallel jobs and to stop the two identifier controls
from paying for a kernel replay they do not use. The design below is settled; no consultation is needed.

## Measured (2026-10-02, commit 28bae18, ubuntu-24.04 public runner, 4 CPU)

- Job: 32.5 min.
- `Run all gates`: 285 s. Inside it: dev shell 22 s, Lean build 73 s, then the index, the
  `leanchecker --fresh` replay, render and values in about 185 s, then the other eight gates in 3 s.
- The 71 controls: 1655 s in series.
- `Prove the identifier gate rejects a tag naming a withdrawn id` and `... an undefined id`:
  196 s and 193 s. Each runs the whole formal gate only to get `.lake/index.jsonl`, and the
  replay is most of that time.
- Per-step GitHub times: `/var/tmp/ctl/gh-steps-28bae18.tsv` (number, name, start, end).
- On this machine, four controls at a time peak at 11.7 GB. Each job runs its steps in series,
  so memory is not a constraint.

## 1. `tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`

- The flag skips only the `lake env leanchecker --fresh BtcPolicy` block. Everything else runs
  unchanged and in the same order: the greps, the build, the import walk, the index, render and
  values. When skipped, it prints one line saying the replay was skipped.
- Any other argument is an error that exits 2.
- `tools/check-all.sh` still calls it with no argument, so the full gate always replays.
- The two identifier controls above pass `--no-replay`. No other control changes its call: the
  other eleven expect a failure before the replay is reached.

## 2. `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: four parallel jobs

- Strategy: `fail-fast: false`, `matrix: shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- Job name: `specification gates (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})`.
- Checkout and install-nix run on every shard, with no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` gets `if: matrix.shard == 0`. Its body is unchanged.
- A new step right after it, `if: matrix.shard != 0`, runs
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`. It builds the `.lake` that the
  controls copy, including the index, regions and values that the citation, copies and regions
  controls read.
- Every control step gets exactly one `if: matrix.shard == N` in that literal form, with N in the
  matrix list. Do not reorder, rename or edit the control bodies. The two `--no-replay` edits
  are the only body changes.
- **Balance the shards from the measured times.** Shard 0 carries `Run all gates` (285 s).
  Every other shard carries the formal setup step, estimated at 130 s. Each identifier control
  is estimated at 196 s minus 150 s for the replay. Assign controls longest first (LPT) so the
  four estimated shard totals sit within 10% of their mean. Record the estimated totals in the
  report, not in the repository.

## 3. A guard that every step runs on the shards it should, with its own negative control

Write a small check (a Python script under `tools/`, run in the dev shell) and run it from a step
on shard 0. It fails, with a message naming the step, unless all of these hold:

- The matrix shard list is exactly `[0, 1, …, N-1]`.
- Checkout and install-nix have no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` has `if: matrix.shard == 0`, and its body is exactly
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`.
- The formal setup step has `if: matrix.shard != 0`.
- Every other step has exactly `if: matrix.shard == N`, with N in the list.
- `tools/check-all.sh` does not contain `--no-replay`.

Following this repository's rule that every gate is proven able to fail, add a control step. In a
scratch copy it deletes one control's `if:` line and asserts the guard exits nonzero with the
exact expected message. It also asserts the guard passes on the untouched copy.

## 4. Prose

Grep `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/` for any sentence that the new layout makes
false: one job, steps in order, or every step running on every push. Fix only those sentences.

- `README.md` lines 25 and 40 stay true. CI still runs `check-all.sh`, now on shard 0, and
  still breaks a document on every run.
- `AGENTS.md` keeps "`.github/workflows/gates.yml` holds the list".

No ADR is needed. This is CI layout, not a specification decision.

## Done when

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` passes, run unpiped and alone in the checkout.
- `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <steps>` passes on the working tree
  for the new guard, its control and the two identifier controls. Split the steps into chunks
  that each finish within 10 minutes.
- Each shard is replayed after the commit, in a clean worktree. That replay is the maintainer's
  job, not this one's.
- The guard's control is measured at its exact message.
- One commit. No commit message, and no added line in any file, names a model, a review tool or
  an adviser, or carries a Co-Authored-By trailer. This repository is public.
close_reason: Workflow runs as four shards; identifier controls skip the replay; tools/check_shards.py guards the layout with its own control

title: Inherit: a pair's duress bit is the OR of every arm intent naming it, and any holder decision arms with it (withdraws per-Carrier)
description:
**Decided 2026-10-02 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel: inherit.** A pair has one
duress bit, the OR of the duress bits of every arm intent naming its spend commitment. Any holder
decision on that pair arms with that bit: overlay `arm`, `sweep_active`, the `selected_escapes`
insertion and the freeze. Per-Carrier is the withdrawn reading. `DUR-10` already applies the same
OR to the Escape entry: "the entry's duress bit becomes the OR of its old value and the new
intent's, so a normal-PIN replay can never clear a duress authorization".

**Why.** `DUR-4` keys intent "by the Carrier identity", and `NCH-31` makes the identity commit to
the plaintext PIN, so two requests for one pair are two Carriers. Under per-Carrier, whichever
reaches `t` first decides.

On the current kernel, from `Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.w0`, this trace releases the coerced hot
partial on an unarmed node:
1. `accept 10 true … c1 e1`;
2. `accept 11 false … c1 e1`;
3. `receipt 11 1`;
4. `firePass`.

The release does not need the normal PIN. `SPN-5`'s gate table stages a `BAD_PIN` refusal at gate
14 (row 14: `consumed`, `yes`, `yes`), and `DUR-4`'s intent holds "its two commitment ids". If a
wrong-PIN Carrier names a resident pair, its holder decision opens it. That breaks `SEC-24`'s
"flooding wrong PINs produces denial and never an unfrozen quorum". The set does not say whether
a gate-12 intent has its commitment ids before the PSBTs decode at gate 17. Inherit closes the
path either way: a node holding the duress intent arms, and a node without it has no pair a
refused request registered.

Freezing without arming was rejected. It makes the node freeze while unarmed and inside the
horizon, which `DUR-1` forbids. Three readers built that rule independently, and `Silence.silence`
failed on `NodeInv.unfrozen`. Two readers independently built inherit:
- `check-all.sh` passes, `Silence.silence` proves, and no exhibit goes red;
- the trace above arms the node, freezes the hot candidate, and releases only the Escape partial
  past the horizon;
- the combined patch with `bps-8s0.29`'s fix also passes.

**Wanted.** Land inherit as a `Kernel.Rules` guard parameter, with per-Carrier as the withdrawn
value. The trace above goes in `Exhibits.lean` as its twin, with a flip step in
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` and its error count measured. Text changes:
- `DUR-5`: "write the overlay with `arm = intent.duress`" becomes the pair's duress bit, and
  "add the pair's Escape to `selected_escapes` with the intent's duress bit (`DUR-10`)" becomes
  "with the pair's duress bit".
- `SPN-23`: "re-applies its schedule and intent, and re-stages" becomes "re-applies its schedule,
  records its own intent (`DUR-4`), and re-stages". Add the converse of its duress-resubmission
  sentence: a resubmission whose pair a duress intent names arms at its own holder decision.
- `SPN-37`: "opened only by its own Carrier's holder decision (`DUR-5`)" becomes "opened only by
  the holder decision of a Carrier naming it (`DUR-5`)". Make the matching change to `DUR-8`'s
  "waits for its own Carrier's holder decision".
- `CNF-29`: add the converse case.
- `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4: dated amendment of "arming is a receipt reaching `t` on a
  Carrier whose intent bit is set".
- `CONTEXT.md`, written after the rule lands:
  - *Release gate*: "opens only on the candidate's own holder decision" becomes "opens only on
    the holder decision of a Carrier naming the candidate's pair".
  - A new *Pair duress bit* entry.
  - *Arm intent*: notes that two Carriers over one pair carry separate intents, and the pair acts
    on their OR.

**`T`'s start (decided).** `DUR-13`'s `first_seen` is the earliest `first_seen` among every arm
intent naming the pair, under both PINs. A later copy must not stretch the hostage window, which
`DUR-13` forbids: "so that slow or selective delivery cannot stretch the hostage window". Taking
the earliest of the duress intents only would make `T` depend on the PIN. Amend `DUR-13`'s "from
the intent's `first_seen`" to match. In `Kernel.newDeadline`, the minimum is read over the
Carriers naming `k.spend`.

**Sticky, on the nonce tombstone (decided).** Inherit's bit must outlive an intent that retires
uncommitted.

On correct clocks, an intent's `D` can lapse before the pair's `E`. `NCH-33` samples `M` "before
authentication", so a wait for the lock shortens `D`. A normal copy accepted while A is resident
can then reach `t` after A retires, and under resident-only inherit it releases. Two readers built
the trace.

The record that already outlives the intent is the nonce tombstone. `NCH-40` says it "keeps `D`
and remains a capacity entry until both wall expiry and `D` have ended". That lifetime is the
window in which a copy of the pair can still be admitted (`SPN-10`: "`expiry > effective_now`").
Storing the bit there:
- adds no store;
- leaves `SPN-32`'s "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is" intact;
- keeps `NCH-34`, because the tombstone confers no holder authority.

Text:
- `NCH-40`: the tombstone keeps, from retirement, the intent's duress bit, `first_seen` and two
  commitment ids, conferring no holder authority (`NCH-34`).
- `DUR-5` and `DUR-13`: the pair's duress bit and `first_seen` range over this intent, every
  resident intent, and every tombstone naming the same spend commitment, under both PINs.
- `DUR-12`: "when the duress Carrier confirms" becomes "at a holder decision on a pair whose
  duress bit is set".
- `DUR-34`: "If the Carrier reaches fewer than `t` nodes, nobody arms" holds only on nodes that
  never recorded the duress intent. A later accepted Carrier naming the marked pair arms there.
- `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: the `DEF-1` control's sed must still match once `Kernel.Rules`
  gains the retirement field.
- Add a resident-only flip, red on the censor trace only, with its count measured.

**Refused Carriers** are `bps-8s0.34`: an intent names a pair only once `SPN-23` has computed it,
and a refused Carrier's holder decision opens nothing.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round3-carrier/` (inherit) and
`.context/vault-review-1002/round4-sticky/` (sticky; one reader's patch builds the tombstone shape
with `check-all.sh` green and `Silence.silence` proving).

title: POL-4's beyond-max theorem has premises the documented derive cannot meet, and POL-4's skip rule has no model
description:
`BtcPolicy.Membership.not_matches_beyond_max` is the formal home of the upper end of `POL-4`'s
"derive indices `0..=max` if it has a wildcard", which `CNF-15` tests as "not at `max + 1`". Both
of its premises range over every `SinglePath`, not over `d.paths`:

- `hdistinct : ∀ p q, p ≠ q → ∀ i j, derive p i ≠ derive q j` fails for every `derive` that reads
  only `id`. `SinglePath`'s docstring calls `id` "its identity (keys, origin, script context —
  everything `derive` reads)", so two paths that differ only in `wildcard` derive the same scripts.
- `hinj : ∀ p i j, derive p i = derive p j → i = j` fails for every `derive` that is constant in
  the index on a definite path. `POL-4` says "A definite descriptor ignores `max`".

The two premises can both hold, but only for a `derive` that also reads `wildcard` and puts
distinct scripts at definite-path indices no scan reads. So the theorem is not vacuous in the
abstract; it is vacuous under the module's own description of `derive`. Its premise `_hp` is
unused, and no exhibit instantiates it.

Second, `POL-4` says "An index the library cannot derive is skipped", but
`derive : SinglePath → Nat → Script` is total, so a failed derivation has to be some script. An
empty-script sentinel matches an empty output script. The module docstring's "The structure
covered is the whole of what `POL-4` requires beyond that boundary" is therefore not yet true.

Wanted:
- `derive : SinglePath → Nat → Option Script`, where a failed derivation contributes no match.
- `matchesScript derive max d s = true ↔ ∃ p ∈ d.paths, ∃ i ∈ indices max p, derive p i = some s`.
- The bound stated as locality, with no premise and over the bound itself: two `derive`s that agree
  on every `p ∈ d.paths` and every `i ≤ max` give the same `matchesScript`.
  - Do not state it over `i ∈ indices max p`. That form still proves when the wildcard range is
    `List.range (max + 2)`, so it does not pin the bound.
- `not_matches_beyond_max` kept as `CNF-15`'s formal home, restated for a wildcard path only:
  `p ∈ d.paths` with `p.wildcard = true`. Its premises are that `derive p (max + 1)` differs from
  every `derive q i` with `q ∈ d.paths` and `i ∈ indices max q`. That is local to `d`, and a
  `derive` constant in the index on definite paths meets it. Add an exhibit that instantiates it.
  - The wildcard condition is required, not optional. On a definite path, a `derive` that ignores
    the index has `derive p (max + 1) = derive p 0`, which the scan reads, so the old conclusion is
    false there. `CNF-15`'s "not at `max + 1`" is about wildcard scans in any case.
- An exhibit that a `derive` returning `none` everywhere matches nothing.
- `kindOf` and `member_discharged` carried over, unchanged in meaning.

Evidence: reviewers A, B, C and D of the 2026-10-02 reading, each with scratch builds. The
off-by-one mutation and both locality forms were compiled. The exhibits above land those probes in
the repository.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- in a scratch copy, changing the wildcard range in `indices` to `List.range (max + 2)` turns a
  `POL-4`-tagged theorem red;
- every `POL-4`-tagged theorem that has a premise has an exhibit instantiating it.

title: CHN-11's sighash has no BIP143 instance, but the Kernel docstring and ADR-0023 item 4 say milestone 5 supplied one
description:
`CHN-11`'s sighash has no instance, and two records say it does. The `Kernel` module docstring
and `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4 both say "milestone 5 supplies the BIP143 encoder as its
instance". Milestone 5 (`bps-8s0.5`) never listed a BIP143 encoder and closed without one: its
six tickets are `Encode`, the `CHN-24` edit, `CoordRequest`, `Manifest`, `Witness` and the
packaging test. The sentence entered with milestone 4.

Item 4 also calls the sighash "a structure whose field is a function of the transaction and the
input index". In the code, `BtcPolicy.Kernel.sighash` is a plain `def` over
`abbrev Sighash := Nat × Nat`, so there is nowhere for an instance to plug in.

Because the declaration carries `@[req "CHN-11"]`, the requirement index lists `CHN-11` against
`sighash` alone. What `sighash` actually formalizes is one property of `CHN-11`: the message is a
function of the transaction and the input, "and of no request field". It does not formalize
`CHN-11`'s "BIP143 P2WSH sighash computed with `SIGHASH_ALL` … with the input's `witness_utxo`
value".

The defect is in the accepted ADR's record of what milestone 5 delivered and what the boundary is.
Correcting the code comment alone would be cosmetic.

Wanted:
- `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4 and the `Kernel` docstring name the BIP143 instance as an open
  boundary, not a milestone-5 deliverable.
- Item 4 describes the sighash as it is: a fixed symbolic definition, not a pluggable structure.
- `sighash`'s docstring says which part of `CHN-11` it formalizes and which part is the boundary.

Building a BIP143 framing encoder is a separate `ADR-0023` decision and out of scope here.
`Encode`'s docstring already records why framing stops at the digest: "(decision 3, and the bead:
no SHA-256 in Lean)". Framing alone would prove a field layout and nothing about binding.

Done when `tools/check-all.sh` is green and neither record claims an instance or a structure the
formal layer lacks.

title: Kernel accept re-registers a resident pair: a fresh-nonce resubmission revives a claw-back-defeated hot spend
description:
`BtcPolicy.Kernel.accept` re-registers a resident pair, so a fresh-nonce resubmission revives a hot
spend that a claw-back has defeated.

`SPN-32` owns the rule: "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is" and "a
conflicting resident commitment is `PSBT_INCONSISTENT` / `candidate_identity`". `SPN-23`'s replay
"re-stages", and staging belongs to the Carrier: per `SPN-32`, the node "stages the Carrier — pushes
the request to the outbox and counts itself as a holder".

Beside its lockdown guard, `accept` checks resident Carrier ids but not resident candidate ids. On a resubmission it prepends fresh `born` copies with `terminal := false` and
`released := false`.

Trace on the current kernel, from `Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.w0`:
1. `accept 10 false … c1 e1`;
2. `settle claw`, which marks candidate 1 terminal;
3. `accept 11 false … c1 e1`, the same pair under a fresh nonce;
4. `receipt 11 1`;
5. a fire pass after the claw-back is evicted.

The pass emits `queuePartial (sighash tx1 0) 0 true 1`, and a terminal copy of candidate 1 is still
resident. Without step 3 the pass emits nothing.

That is `F57`'s defect class in the model. `SPN-33` says "a hot spend a claw-back has defeated is
not finalized at its Hold expiry even if the claw-back is later evicted", and `terminal_sticky`'s
own disjunct, "or was born by this step", admits the revival. The guard does not read the PIN.

`accept` also takes `sp.id = es.id` and registers two candidates under one id.

Wanted:
- An accept whose pair is resident, with equal `tx`, `hot` and `expiry`, adds its Carrier and
  leaves the candidates exactly as is.
- A resident id with any other field, or `sp.id = es.id`, is refused.
- Say whether a replay still runs `DUR-14`'s shrink and `DUR-20`'s traversal, since `SPN-23` says
  it "re-applies its schedule".
- A theorem: on every `Reachable` world, one id names at most one resident candidate.
- `terminal_sticky` restated so that a resident terminal id is never matched by a non-terminal
  candidate.
- The trace above as an exhibit that releases nothing under `current`, plus a same-PIN and a
  cross-PIN replay that leave the resident candidates' `terminal`, `released` and `heldSigners`
  untouched.

Evidence: reviewer B (scratch builds, with the control run), reviewers C and D (same-PIN
duplication).

title: silence's relation stops at a resubmission after its pair's holder decision: wfEvent refuses SPN-23's repeat
description:
`BtcPolicy.Silence.silence`'s relation stops at a resubmission.

`obsPair` walks a trace only while `wfEvent` holds. `wfEvent` refuses an accept whose candidate ids
are already in `selected`, and `selected` holds Escape ids, which a holder decision inserts. So a
resubmission after its pair's holder decision ends the walk; an earlier one is walked.
`wfEvent`'s docstring justifies the refusal as requiring "what the identifiers intend". But `SPN-23`
specifies that repeat: a request whose acceptance key matches an earlier `Accepted` "re-applies its
schedule and intent, and re-stages".

`DUR-15` says a post-wrench coordinator "can mint validly signed requests indefinitely". So it can
end the relation's coverage at a step of its choosing, inside the concealment horizon.

Reviewer B ran `armTrace` plus one resubmission. Both entering states are `preHorizon`, `wfEvent`
is false, and the walk yields 2 observation pairs instead of 4. A walk without the guard gives equal
observations at all four steps, so this is a coverage gap, not a leak.

Wanted: once `bps-8s0.29` makes `accept` leave a resident pair as is, replace `wfEvent`'s repeat
conjuncts with the uniqueness invariant that bead proves. Then state `silence` over traces that
include resubmissions.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- an exhibit replaying `armTrace` plus a resubmission yields an observation pair for every
  pre-horizon step, the resubmission included, and proves them equal (equality over a truncated
  walk does not count);
- the existing `DUR-1` exhibits still prove;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: silence's starting premises cannot be derived from Reachable: Reachable.init leaves sweepActive free
description:
`silence`'s starting premises cannot be derived from `Reachable`, because
`BtcPolicy.Kernel.Reachable.init` pins only `armed = false`, `cands = []` and `carriers = []`. It
leaves `sweepActive` free, so a node with `armed = false`, `sweepActive = true` and
`selected = [(7, true)]` is `Reachable`, and it fails `Silence.NodeInv`'s sweep clause (reviewers A
and C, compiled).

`silence` takes `NodeInv` at the trace's first sample, "assumed here and not derived from
reachability", and `Exhibits.TwoRun.nodeInv_A` discharges it for one concrete start only.

No theorem is false. `holderDecision` sets `armed` and `sweepActive` with the same `|| k.duress`,
so `sweepActive = armed` is preserved by every event (compiled), but nothing states it. This is a
missing invariant, not a bug.

Wanted:
- `Reachable.init` pins `sweepActive = false`. Pinning `selected = []` as well is optional: the
  corollary below does not need it.
- A theorem `sweepActive = armed` over `Reachable`.
- `no_entry_released_before_arming` restated over `armed = false`.
- A corollary, after `Init.silence_from_init` in `.context/vault-review-1002/probes/Init.lean`:
  `silence` for two runs from the same node, the same ledger and empty exposure, with
  `armed = false`, `sweepActive = false` and empty candidates. The rule and monotone-sample
  hypotheses stay explicit.

This establishes initialization only, not `NodeInv` for every `Reachable` state. Pinning `init`
removes worlds from every `Reachable` theorem, which is intended: the removed worlds have
`selected` entries that no accepted Carrier put there.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- the guard-parameter flips in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still fail at their asserted
  `Exhibits.lean` sites;
- the corollary is tagged `DUR-1`.
close_reason: Below the filing bar: no theorem is false and the invariant already holds per step. Silence.NodeInv.sweep is sweepActive = armed and inv_sysStep preserves it on every event. Mutating holderDecision so a duress commit no longer sets sweepActive goes red in Silence.lean today, so pinning Reachable.init adds no catching power.

title: DUR-8's coupling has no theorem: prove hot-release provenance at input 0 and the counting corollary
description:
`DUR-8` says "So no honest node ever releases a coerced partial, only `≤ t − 1` compromised nodes
can, and that is never a signing quorum. This coupling, not the holder count, is the safety proof".
No declaration states it. The `Kernel` docstring says "`DUR-8`'s federation consequence is a
counting statement under `compromised < t`, not a theorem here", and `no_hot_partial_while_armed`
covers armed nodes only.

Wanted, node-local and at input 0, with no federation and no scheduler:
- **Provenance.** On every reachable world, a hot `queuePartial` for candidate `cid` is emitted
  only by an unarmed node, and only after a normal-PIN holder decision that opened `cid`, tied to
  the emitted message and commitment. Prove it over the event trace or recorded commit history:
  `holderDecision` retires the Carrier, so the Carrier need not stay resident. A ghost field on
  `Node` changes every `Node` literal in `Exhibits.lean`.
- **Counting corollary over the world's exposure.** The premise that every honest exposure row for
  a message carries that provenance is a named hypothesis, since `adversaryExposes` and
  `receivePartial` admit any signer. Under that premise, with no honest normal holder decision for
  the message and fewer than `t` distinct compromised signers, `exposedQuorum` is false for it.

Input 0 is enough for prevention. Under `SIGHASH_ALL`, `DUR-28`'s "`≥ t` distinct valid partials
on every input" makes a quorum at input 0 necessary for finalization, so counting there
over-approximates availability (reviewers A and B).

On an unarmed node every committed Carrier is normal-PIN: `holderDecision` sets
`armed := n.armed || k.duress`. So the statement holds on the current kernel and needs neither
`bps-8s0.26` nor `bps-8s0.31`.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- both theorems are tagged `DUR-8`;
- an exhibit instantiates the corollary at a concrete world, and another shows a successful normal
  release;
- a twin in which quorum opens without a holder decision refutes the provenance statement;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: A refused-but-staged Carrier's holder decision opens a resident pair: DUR-4 names commitment ids before SPN-23 computes them
description:
**Decided 2026-10-02 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel, which agreed unanimously.**
1. An arm intent names a pair only once `SPN-23` has computed the pair's commitments.
2. The holder decision of a refused Carrier opens nothing. A refused Carrier carrying a duress
   intent still arms.

**The defect.** `DUR-4` says the intent recorded at ingress (`SPN-5` gate 12) holds "its two
commitment ids". But the PSBTs decode at gate 17, and `SPN-23` computes the commitments "After all
preceding admission, PIN and post-preflight clock gates pass". The set never says when a gate-12
intent learns its ids.

`SPN-5`'s gate table stages some refusals: they consume the nonce, propagate and stage.
- **Before `SPN-23`:** gate 13 and 16 (clock predicates) and gate 14 (`BAD_PIN`). Read literally,
  `DUR-4` lets such an intent name a pair.
- **After `SPN-23`:** gate 21 (prevout fetch), gate 22 (only `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`), gate 24
  (`HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED`) and gate 27 (`EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` / `commitment_expiry`). These do name
  a pair.

`DUR-5`'s holder decision sets "`holder_quorum_reached` on both members of the pair, which opens
their release gate". So a refused Carrier that reaches `t` holders opens a resident pair that
this node refused to authorize, though `SPN-9` says "Neither path signs a partial". A gate-14
refusal needs no valid PIN at all. That contradicts `SEC-24`: "flooding wrong PINs produces denial
and never an unfrozen quorum".

**Wanted.**
- `DUR-4`: "its two commitment ids" becomes "its two commitment ids once `SPN-23` has computed
  them; an intent refused before then names no pair".
- `DUR-5`: a holder decision opens the pair only for a Carrier this node accepted, or replayed as
  accepted (`SPN-23`). For a refused Carrier it performs the same arm write, scan and set work
  under both PINs, and opens no candidate. It still arms with the duress bit, as `SEC-24` requires
  ("MUST arm regardless of lockout") and as `DUR-4` requires ("the duress bit MUST be set for a
  refused-but-staged duress request just as for an accepted one").
- `DUR-10`: "**Every** holder decision adds its intent's Escape id" applies only when the intent
  names a pair.
- The kernel gains a refused-but-staged acceptance event. A theorem states that its holder
  decision opens no candidate, with an exhibit replaying a staged refusal that reaches `t`.
- The `DUR-1` relation covers the new event.

**Interaction.** Independent of `bps-8s0.26`'s inherit rule, and needed under every reading. One
reader judged inherit's sticky extension unnecessary once this lands, so decide this before the
sticky question.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round4-sticky/` (briefs, four answers, four prototype
patches).

- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count;
- the staged-refusal exhibit opens nothing under `current`.
